finding: The live range of $200-$1,125 is about right at the top and a little low at the bottom; it is wide because the vehicle classes really do differ this much. Built totals (parts + stated hours x $120-$160/hr, the national middle labor rate used for these checks): economy 2015 Corolla about $230-$723 (0.9-2.0 hr); midsize 2016 Camry about $240-$545 (0.9-2.0 hr); truck 2016 F-150 5.0L about $275-$683 (1.0-2.0 hr); luxury 2015 BMW 328i about $416-$1,057 (1.6-2.0 hr). The lowest total we can build is about $230, and that uses a remanufactured starter at an online price ($122) plus a manufacturer warranty time, which is less than a shop normally charges for either; the lowest benchmark is $350 (AAA). So $200 is below anything found and roughly $230-$250 is the supportable floor. The $1,125 ceiling fits: a genuine BMW starter at list ($737) plus 2 hours comes to about $1,057, and AAA's top figure is $1,100. How solid the labor times are: the low ends for the economy and midsize classes are Honda warranty flat-rate times for comparable cars (0.9 hr for a 2012 Civic and for a 2013-2016 Accord V6), not Toyota times; the luxury low end is a BMW bulletin allowance for the same-body 330e plug-in hybrid (16 FRU, 1.6 hr at 10 FRU per hour, a conversion that rests on two informal technician sources), not the 328i's N20 engine; the truck figures are a parts seller's 2-hour estimate and a general 1-2 hour statement. The high ends use parts retailers' general statement that a starter typically takes one to two hours; the same guides say hard-to-reach starters can take 3-4 hours or more, so some vehicles will exceed these totals. Our mainstream totals sit below RepairPal ($565-$796) and Kelley Blue Book ($728-$820); the gap is mostly in parts, since our low ends use remanufactured units at online prices ($122-$155) while RepairPal's parts figure is $375-$516.
extras: A quote often adds a starting and charging system test or diagnosis fee, a refundable core charge on a remanufactured starter (about $35-$85 on the listings seen), shop supplies, and sales tax. A weak battery or corroded battery cables are often found at the same time and quoted separately. On engines where the starter sits under the intake manifold, new intake gaskets may be added.
